title: Startup write probe pattern is correct for IAM validation
description: Running a PUT + DELETE probe at startup to verify bucket/container write access and IAM permissions before accepting articles is the correct operational pattern. It fails fast, surfaces permission errors with context (which account/bucket/prefix) before any article is processed, and exercises prefix-scoped IAM policies that a plain authentication check would not catch. A contributor might suggest removing it as 'unnecessary' (the operation will fail on first real write anyway). This should be resisted — the probe gives a clear error at startup rather than a silent first-article failure hours later.
